To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

There is a paucity of published research regarding interventions to support people living with rheumatoid disease (RA) during their reproductive years; only one study evaluated a motherhood decision-making intervention for RA, and only one study incorporated information on contraception and fertility; there are opportunities to develop targeted resources to support people with rheumatological conditions during their reproductive years.

“We found no published studies evaluating the effectiveness of interventions designed to improve knowledge of and/or self-management strategies relating to family planning and pregnancy in people with RA, although we did identify a number of studies that incorporated relevant components within broader RA education or self-management programmes”.
there is a need for RA-specific information on family planning and pregnancy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the provision of education to people with rheumatological conditions to help them make decisions about family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding.
how people with RA can be better supported in making informed decisions about their reproductive health.
the provision of information regarding contraception, pregnancy and lactation to patients with rheumatoid disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is insufficient evidence to make any conclusions on the effectiveness of any interventions to improve knowledge concerning contraception, pregnancy or breastfeeding in people with RA.
there is no conclusive evidence that any intervention to improve knowledge and skills concerning family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding is effective.

there are no interventions that are known to be effective for improving the knowledge and/or self management skills of people with rheumatology conditions concerning contraception, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a lack of information on family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding for people with RA.
there is no research on interventions for improving knowledge or skills concerning contraception, family planning, pregnancy and breastfeeding.
there is a need for further research into the impact of RA on reproductive health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current evidence base is insufficient to support the development of interventions to improve the knowledge and self-management of women with RA during their childbearing years.
the field is lacking in terms of interventions for women with RA during the reproductive years.
the current evidence base for RA educational and self-management interventions is limited.
